paragraphs.text: In a dry region of the south-west, a town council decided in 2018 that new houses could not have grass in their front gardens. Existing lawns were allowed, but no new ones could be laid.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Water use fell by a tenth within three years. Most of the saving came from a few large gardens rather than from many small ones, because the largest users had been watering daily.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Gardeners found substitutes. Gravel with drought-tolerant shrubs is the commonest, though some households chose a small paved terrace with pots that can be moved into shade.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The rule has critics. Older residents say that a green lawn cooled the street, and measurements show that gravel gardens are indeed several degrees warmer in the afternoon.
paragraphs.label: D

headings.text: A drawback of the new gardens
